The ovary is inferior with 2 locules containing numerous ovules. The fruit is a capsule at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Bromelia pinguin grows without discernible stems up to 1 m (excluding inflorescence) in height. The leaves dark green adaxially and whitish abaxially, organized in a rosette forming a series of cups at their base that can hold water and detritus. The leaves are parallel veined, lanceolate, deeply serrated margin, with recurved spines up to 1 cm long, and to 6 cm wide at the base and up to 2 m in length with a spined leaf apex. The complete, perfect, slightly zygomorphic flowers, each with a subtending bract, are arranged in a white, tomentose, spikelike panicle. The lower bracts below the inflorescence are bright red colored. The flowers have 3 white tomentose fused sepals in the calyx that exceed the length of the bracts. There are 3 red with white margins, fused at the base petals in the corolla that are longer than the calyx. There are 6 stamens that are equal in length and adnate to the petals. The ovary is inferior with 3 locules and numerous seeds. The fruit is a yellow berry at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Phoradendron racemosum grows as a parasite on other trees and shrubs with round stems. The leaves are arranged oppositely, to 9 cm in length, ovate to elliptic to lanceolate, with an obtuse to retuse leaf apex. The petioles are winged. Phoradendron racemosum is monoecious. The highly reduced, incomplete, imperfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in jointed spikes. The flowers partially embedded in the rachis. In staminate flowers there are 3 tepals, 3 stamens and no carpel. In carpellate flowers there are 3 tepals, no stamens, and 1 inferior ovary and 1 ovule. The fruit is a white drupe at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Pisonia aculeata grows as a viney shrub/subtree/liana, with ascending inflorescences, spreading outward up to 7 m and often climbing on and out from other vegetation. The simple leaves are arranged oppositely, ovate to cordate, to 12 cm in length, with a sinuate leaf margin and an acute/acuminate/obtuse leaf apex. Spines occur at the nodes and are up to 4 cm in length. Pisonia aculeata is monoecious. The incomplete, imperfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in a cymose panicle. The calyx has 5, fused into a cup, sepals that are white. There are no petals. In staminate flowers there are 10 stamens and a non-functional carpel. In carpellate flowers there are 10 non-functional stamens with a superior ovary with 1 locule and ovule. The fruit is a 5 ribbed achene that is retained within the glandular calyx at maturity (anthocarp).
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Passiflora foetida grows as vine with older portions of the stem becoming slightly corky at the base with age. Vegetation has glandular pubescence. The cordate leaves are arranged alternately, to 12 cm in length, 3 to 5 lobed, often with a slightly crenate margin. The lobes are elliptic to oblong. At the top of the petiole are 2 round glands. Tendrils are present at the nodes. The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged are solitary in leaf axils. There are 2 -4 pinnatifid bracts below the flower with glands at their tips. The calyx has 5 green unfused sepals. There is no corolla. There is a corona with filaments in 2 series. The outer series is white/pink/purple with purple veins and recurved. The inner series is filamentous and is white or purple with a maroon/red base. There are 5 stamens. The ovary is superior, with 3 stigmatic lobes, a single locule and numerous seeds. The fruit is a berry that turns red/orange/yellow at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Passiflora edulis grows as vine with older portions becoming corky with age. The 3 – lobed leaves are arranged alternately, to 15 cm in length and a crenate/serrate margin. The lobes are elliptic to oblong. At the top of the petiole are 2 round glands. Tendrils are present at the nodes. The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in pairs or are solitary in leaf axils. There are pinnatifid bracts below the flower. The calyx has 5 green unfused sepals. There is no corolla. There is a corona with filaments in 2 series. The outer series is white and recurved. The inner series is filamentous and is white with a maroon/red base. There are 5 stamens. The ovary is superior, with 3 stigmatic lobes, a single locule and numerous seeds. The fruit is a berry that turns yellow at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: hytolacca icosandra grows as long-lived perennial becoming slightly woody at stem base to 3 m in height. The leaves are arranged alternately, to 25 cm in length, elliptic to lanceolate to ovate, with an acute (sometimes mucronate) leaf apex and entire margin. The incomplete, perfect, actinomorphic, flowers are arranged in axillary and terminal spike like, slightly pubescent, racemes. The calyx has 5 greenish white to pink unfused, sepals subtended by two bracts. There are no petals. There are numerous unfused stamens. The there are numerous united carpels. The fruit is a purple berry at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Bursera inaguensis grows as a small to medium tree up to 5 m in height and a trunk to 50 cm. The bark is grey and smooth and does not peal. The pinnately compound leaves are arranged alternately and are clustered at branch tips with 5-7 leaflets. The leaflets are oblanceolate to oblong with a apiculate leaf apex and entire leaf margin. Bursera inaguensis is dioecious. The actinomorphic, incomplete, imperfect, flowers are arranged in short branched panicles. Staminate flowers have 5 fused, green sepals, 5 yellow green unfused petals, 10 unfused stamens, and an infertile superior ovary. Carpellate flowers have 3 partially fused sepals, 3 yellow green, unfused petals, 7 staminodes and a superior ovary with 3 locules. The fruit is a leathery drupe or 2-seeded berry at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Cardamine flexuosa grows as a glabrous to densely hirsute, erect to decumbent, biennial to perennial herb to 75 cm in height when in flower/fruit, usually smaller. The bipinnate, alternate leaves sometimes in a basal rosette, to 10 cm in length. Terminal leaflet ovate to 2 cm long, 2-5 lobed, round to reniform. Lateral leaflets ovate to elliptic, 2-5 lobed, and to 1 cm in width. The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are in terminal and axillary racemes up to 50 centimeters in length. The calyx has 4 unfused, green sepals. The corolla has 4 unfused, white to purple petals. There are 6 stamens. The superior ovary with 2 locules separated by an elongate replum. The fruit is an elongate, oval, many seeded silique.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Chromolaena bahamensis a woody perennial shrub to 3 meters in height (usually smaller). Vegetation short pubescent during growth. The leaves are arranged oppositely, to 8 cm in length, lanceolate to ovate, with an entire to slightly crenate leaf margin toward the apex, with a tapering leaf base and rounded to obtuse apex. The leaves are glandular punctuate abaxially and visibly 3 veined.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in corymbs of heads subtended an involucre made of 4-5 series of glandular, lanceolate phyllaries. The calyx is modified as hairs forming a brown pappus. The corolla has 5, fused with light blue to lavender petals with acute lobes. There are 5 stamens fused to the base of the corolla. The ovary is inferior with a single locule. The fruit is an achene at maturity that retains the modified calyx (pappus).
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Argythamnia argentea grows as erect woody herb to 50 cm in height (typically shorter). The leaves are arranged alternately, narrow elliptic, to 5 cm in length with an acute apex, entire to slightly gland tipped serrate along the upper leaf margin. The vegetation has appressed malpighiaceous trichomes and is silvery.

The incomplete, imperfect, monoecious, actinomorphic, flowers are arranged in leaf axils. Staminate flowers with 4 greenish, ovate sepals and acute petals and 4 stamens. Carpellate flowers with 5 greenish, sepals and petals, 5 glands, and a single superior carpel with bi-fid styles, with 3 locules and numerous seeds. The fruit is a capsule at maturity that splits along 3 suture lines. The entire floral structure, including the fruit, is silvery hirsute.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Encyclia caicensis grow as an epiphyte on plants and directly on limestone. It produces a very short rhizomatous stem that is covered with secondary stems that are expanded to form linear lanceolate pseudobulbs up to 15 cm in length and 5 cm in width. From the top of the pseudobulb 4 flattened linear lanceolate leaves emerge that are up to 60 cm in length and 3 cm wide. The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal open panicles up to 2 m in height and contains up to 60 flowers. The flowers have ovate-triangular bracts and the calyx has 3 greenish yellow to tan sepals. The corolla has 3 green to brown to reddish brown petals with lower central one forming the labellum. The sepals and petals turn reddish and develop stripes with age. The labellum is white, with purple stripes, and 3 lobed. The central lobe is to 2 cm long. The 2 lateral lobes/auricles of the labellum are yellow white with radiating purple red lines at their base, erect and appressed/clasping to either side of the column. The central lobe of the labellum is yellow tan/white, with a round/undulate margin and red/purple stripes. The lower third of the labellum is fused to the column. The column is formed from a fusion of the stamens and ovary into a single elongate structure. Along the base of the column between the lateral labellum lobes is a white callus plate with 2 ridges/keels that unite at the front edge with 2 yellow anther lobes. The ovary is inferior. The fruit is a capsule at maturity up to 3 cm in length that opens along six suture lines and hangs pendulant, allowing wind to assist in seed dispersal.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Encyclia inaguensis grow as an epiphyte on plants and directly on limestone. It produces a very short rhizomatous stem that is covered with secondary stems that are expanded to form linear lanceolate pseudobulbs up to 30 cm in length and 3 cm in width. From the top of the pseudobulb 2 flattened linear lanceolate leaves emerge that are up to 60 cm in length and 1.5 cm wide. The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal open panicles up to 150 cm in height and contains up to 50 flowers. The flowers have ovate-triangular bracts and the calyx has 3 green to brown to reddish brown sepals. The corolla has 3 green to brown to reddish brown petals with lower central one forming the labellum. The sepals and petals develop stripes with age. The labellum is white, with purple stripes, and 3 lobed. The central lobe is to 2 cm long. The 2 lateral lobes/auricles of the labellum are white with yellow tips and with radiating purple red lines at their base and ascending away from either side of the column. The central lobe of the labellum is white with a yellow edge, an undulate margin and purple stripes. The lower third of the labellum is fused to the column. The column is formed from a fusion of the stamens and ovary into a single elongate structure. Along the base of the column between the lateral labellum lobes is a ridged callus plate with 2 lobes/teeth at the front edge with the yellow anthers. The ovary is inferior. The fruit is a capsule at maturity up to 3 cm in length that opens along six suture lines and hangs pendulant, allowing wind to assist in seed dispersal.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Encyclia withneri grow as an epiphyte. It produces a very short rhizomatous stem that is covered with secondary stems that are expanded to form ovate pseudobulbs up to 5 cm in length and 3 cm in width. From the top of the pseudobulb 2 flattened linear lanceolate leaves emerge that are up to 25 cm in length and 1.5 cm wide. The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal panicles up to 60 cm in height and contains up to 30 flowers. The pedicels are rough/bumpy. The flowers have ovate-triangular bracts and the calyx has 3 reddish brown sepals. The corolla has 3 reddish brown petals with one forming the labellum. The sepals and petals develop stripes with age. The labellum is white and 3 lobed. The central lobe is to 1.5 cm long. The 2 lateral lobes of the labellum are white with radiating purple red lines at their base and appressed/clasping to either side of the column. The midlobe of the labellum has 3 prominent ridges. The lower third of the labellum is fused to the column. The column is formed from a fusion of the stamens and ovary into a single elongate structure. Along the bottom of the column between the lateral labellum lobes is a ridged callus plate with 3 lobes at the front edge with the yellow anthers. The ovary is inferior. The fruit is a capsule at maturity up to 3 cm in length that opens along six suture lines and hangs pendulant, allowing wind to assist in seed dispersal.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Metastelma inaguense grows as a glabrous, climbing vine to over 3 m in length. The leaves are oppositely arranged, to 7 cm, oblanceolate/obovate/linear, with an entire margin and an obtuse/rounded, sometimes apiculate, leaf apex. The vegetation produces a milky sap.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in axillary cymes. The calyx has 5, unfused, sepals with ovate lobes. The corolla has 5, papillose pubescent internally and glabrous externally, unfused white (with green bases) petals with linear to oblong lobes. There are 5, unfused stamens. Within the flower there are 5, white, attenuate appendages (crown) that arise from the corolla. The superior ovary has 2 locules with many ovules. The fruit is a follicle at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Ateleia popenoei grows as a medium shrub to small tree up to 6 m. in height, usually smaller. Young stems gray with erect, projecting pubescence and obvious lenticels. The odd pinnately compound leaves are alternately (sometimes suboppositely) arranged. There are 5-11 leaflets, each orbicular to ovate to lanceolate, up to 6 cm long and 3 cm wide, with an obtuse to acute leaflet apex, an oblique leaf base, with an entire margin.

The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in axillary racemes. The calyx has 5 greenish, fused, sepals. The white corolla is reduced to a single white cup shaped petal forming the standard. There are 10 subequal, exserted stamens. The ovary is superior and forms a dry slightly inflated single seeded legume at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Metastelma stipitatum grows as a glabrous, climbing viney shrub to over 3 m in length. The vegetation tinged with a reddish-purple color and generally dichotomously branching. The leaves are oppositely arranged, to 3 cm, elliptic to lanceolate, with an entire margin and an acute to acuminate, often apiculate leaf apex. The vegetation produces a milky sap.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in few flowered axillary cymes. The calyx has 5, unfused, sepals with triangular, ovate lobes with a reddish abaxial surface. The corolla has 5, puberulent/pubescent adaxially, reddish petals with lanceolate, acute lobes that have an abaxial red stripe. There are 5, unfused stamens. Within the flower there are 5, white, appendages (crown) that arise from the corolla. The superior ovary has 2 locules with many ovules. The fruit is a follicle at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Metastelma sigmoideum grows as a glabrous, climbing vine to over 3 m in length. The leaves are oppositely arranged, to 3 cm, ovate/elliptic, with an entire margin and an acute to acuminate leaf apex. The vegetation produces a milky sap.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in few flowered axillary cymes. The calyx has 5, unfused, sepals with triangular lobes. The corolla has 5, glabrous, petals with oblong lanceolate with acute lobes. There are 5, unfused stamens. Within the flower there are 5, white, twisted/contorted/reflexed appendages (crown) that arise from the corolla. The superior ovary has 2 locules with many ovules. The fruit is a follicle at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Koanophyllon correlliorum a woody perennial shrub to 3 meters in height. Vegetation pubescent during growth becoming glabrous with age. The leaves are arranged oppositely, to 8 cm in length, oblanceolate to ovate, with a toothed leaf margin toward the apex or entirely entire, with a tapering leaf base and rounded to obtuse apiculate apex. The leaves are glandular punctuate, visible both ad- and abaxially.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in corymbs of heads subtended an involucre made of 2-3 series of glandular phyllaries. The calyx is modified as hairs forming a pappus. The corolla has 5, fused with white to slightly lavender petals with acute lobes. There are 5 stamens fused to the base of the corolla. The ovary is inferior with a single locule. The fruit is an achene at maturity that retains the modified calyx (pappus).
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Aristida correlliae grows as a glabrous, dense clumping perennial to 50 cm in height when flowering with unbranched stems. The conduplicate leaves are arranged alternately, to 25 cm in length (much shorter towards the stem apex) and up to 2 mm wide with a basal sheath extending along the stem. At the point of divergence of the glabrous leaf sheath to the leaf blade is a fine ciliate ligule. The leaves are parallel veined and the lower portions of the leaf blade toward the stem are adaxially finely pubescent.

The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in an erect raceme made of 2-20 appressed, sessile spikelets. At the base of each spikelet are 2, short awned, structures called glumes. The first glume small and the second larger. In each spikelet there are flowering structures each is subtended by 2 additional structures (lemma and palea). The tip of the lemma has 3 erect awns that are of equal length. There are 3-5 florets with 3 stamens and a superior ovary each with a single locule and seed. The fruit is a caryopsis.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Spermacoce capillaris grows as a bushy, semi succulent, perennial up to 40 cm in height spreading to form loose mounds/balls. The sessile leaves are arranged oppositely with toothed stipules between the petioles. The leaves are filiform up to 6 cm long, and 1-2 mm wide with an acute leaf apex and an entire margin. Internodes as long or longer than the leaves.

The, actinomorphic, perfect, complete, flowers occur in small, pubescent heads in the leaf axils and forming terminal heads. A stipular sheath subtends the flowering “head” with many setae. The calyx has 4 unfused, pubescent, triangular, lobed sepals. The corolla has 4 fused pubescent white petals that form a short tube and each with a recurved lobe with a mucronate apex. There are 4 stamens that are fused to the perianth forming a hypanthium. The ovary is inferior with 1 locule and many ovules. The fruit is a capsule at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Stenandrium carolinae grows as an herb to 15 cm in height when in flower. The leaves are arranged in a basal rosette, up to 4 cm in length (including the petiole) and 1 cm wide, oblong to elliptic to lanceolate, with an obtuse to round leaf apex and slightly crenate margins. The leaves and stems are long haired pubescent. The adaxial surface has both large pustulate hairs and smaller non pustulate hairs and the abaxial surface has fewer hairs.

The complete, perfect, zygomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal spikes Each flower subtended by pubescent bracts. The calyx has 5, green unfused, linear, sepals that are slightly fused at their base. The corolla has 5 fused, pink petals in 2 sets (3 upper and side and 2 lower petals). There are 4 stamens fused to the corolla tube. The superior ovary has 2 locules and numerous ovules. The fruit is a capsule at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Stenandrium bracteosum grows as an herb to 20 cm in height when in flower. The leaves are arranged in a basal rosette, up to 7 cm in length (including the petiole) and 1.5 cm wide, oblong to elliptic to obovate, with an obtuse to acute leaf apex and an entire to slightly crenate margins. The leaves and stems are long haired pubescent. The adaxial surface has only large pustulate hairs and the abaxial surface has fewer hairs.

The complete, perfect, zygomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal spikes. Each flower subtended by pubescent bracts. The calyx has 5, green unfused, linear, sepals that are slightly fused at their base. The corolla has 5 fused, pink petals in 2 sets (3 upper and side and 2 lower petals). There are 4 stamens fused to the corolla tube. The superior ovary has 2 locules and numerous ovules. The fruit is a capsule at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Lepidium filicaule grows as an annual herb, often prostrate, to 15 cm in height when in flower/fruit. Plants can be simple and unbranched or branched toward the base. The leaves sparse toward the base, to 6 cm in length 2 cm wide (usually smaller and narrower), pinnatifid to lobed, narrowing to the petiole. Leaves along the stem smaller and serrulate than basal leaves. Vegetation is sparsely hirsute.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are in terminal and axillary racemes up to 10 centimeters in length. The calyx has 4 unfused, green, caducous sepals. The corolla has 4 unfused, small (sometimes absent) petals. There are 2 stamens and 4 staminodes/glands. The superior ovary with 2 locules separated by a narrow replum. The fruit is a flat, oval, 2 seeded silicle with a notched sinus at the apex.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Ptycanthera correllii grows as a glabrous to thinly hirsute, climbing vine to over 8 m in length. The leaves are oppositely arranged, to 8 cm, triangular to lanceolate, and an acute to obtuse leaf apex and truncate leaf base. The vegetation produces a milky sap.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in few flowered axillary cymes. The calyx has 5, unfused, sepals with triangular lobes. The corolla has 5, glabrous, yellow green with distinct venation, rotate, petals with oblong elliptic with ovate lobes. There are 5, unfused stamens. Within the flower there is a 5 sided, white, appendage (crown) that arise from the corolla. The superior ovary has 2 locules with many ovules. The seeds flat and plumed with hairs. The fruit is an ovoid, winged, follicle at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Evolvulus bahamensis grows as a low, highly branched shrub becoming basally woody, to 50 cm in height. The leaves are arranged alternately, sessile, narrow lanceolate/linear, to oblanceolate, to 1 cm long and 4 mm wide with an entire margin, an acute leaf apex and leaf base. Leaves become scale like toward the stem apex. Vegetation sparsely pubescent.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are solitary in leaf axils. The calyx has 5 unfused, green sepals. The sharply funnelform corolla has 5 fused, light blue to purple/dark petals, sometimes white. There are 5 functional stamens fused to the base of the corolla and 5 staminodes. The superior ovary with 2 locules and numerous ovules. The round fruit is a round, tan, many seeded, pubescent capsule with brown seeds.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Ageratum conyzoides grows as an annual herb to 60 cm in height when in flower. The leaves are arranged oppositely, to 9 cm in length (usually smaller), up to 6 cm wide, triangular to ovate to cordate with an obtuse leaf apex and a crenate margin. The leaves and stems have a covering of pubescence.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal cymes of heads. The head is subtended by glandular pubescent phyllaries forming an involucre in 2 series. The calyx is reduced to bristles (pappus). The corolla has 5, fused, blue to lavender pubescent petals. There are 5, purplish blue stamens that are fused to the inside of the corolla tube. The inferior ovary has a single locule. The fruit is an angular achene with ridges along the edges.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Brya ebenus grows as a winter deciduous tree up to 8 m in height. The bipinnately compound leaves are arranged alternately. The petioles have a slightly swollen pulvinus. The leaflets are in 1-2 dense pairs on reduced branches with leaflets appearing as simple leaves. Each leaflet to 3 cm in length, elliptic to oval, with a round to acute leaf apex, with an entire margin.

The complete, perfect, zygomorphic flowers are arranged in axillary racemes. The calyx has 5 greenish, unfused, oblong sepals. The corolla has 5 yellow, unfused petals, the lower two forming a keel, the upper a banner and the 2 lateral petals as wings. There are 10 stamens (9+1 arrangement). The ovary is superior and forms an elongate, pendulous, many-seeded dark brown legume at maturity up to 60 cm in length and 3 cm in width.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Bismarckia nobilis grows as a medium sized, single trunk tree up to 15 m in height and to 50 cm in diameter. The bark is ringed. The dark green leaves are arranged spirally at the top of the trunk. The leaves are costa palmate, to 3 m in length and width. The outer portions of the lamina divided to about 1/3rd. The petioles are to 3 m in length.

Bismarckia nobilis is dioecious. The incomplete, imperfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in a large panicle that arises below the lowest leaf. The calyx has 3 sepals and the corolla has 3 petals. The calyx and corolla are white and fused together forming a single whorl. Staminate flowers have 7-9 stamens and no carpel. The carpellate flowers have staminodes and a single ovary and ovule. The ovary is superior with a single locule and seed. The fruit is a drupe that is dark brown at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Aristida vilfifolia grows as a glabrous, clumping perennial to 80 cm in height when flowering with unbranched stems. The leaves are arranged alternately, to 8 cm in length, up to 1 mm wide, twisted/curved with a basal sheath extending along the stem. At the point of divergence of the glabrous leaf sheath to the leaf blade is a short ligule. The leaves are parallel veined and the lower portions of the leaf blade toward the stem are adaxially finely pubescent.

The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in an erect narrow panicle made of 2-20 appressed, sessile spikelets. At the base of each spikelet are 2, short awned, structures called glume that are close to equal in size. In each spikelet there are flowering structures each is subtended by 2 additional structures (lemma and palea). The tip of the lemma has 3 spreading twisted awns with the two lateral awns shorter than the central awn. Awns to 2 cm in length. There are 3-5 florets with 3 stamens and a superior ovary each with a single locule and seed. The fruit is a caryopsis.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Asplenium nidus grows from a short rhizome as an epiphyte or terrestrially. Glabrous subsessile fronds numerous from the rhizome appearing top form a rosette. Each frond linear/lanceolate, up to 150 cm in length and 20 cm wide, with an entire margin and acute apex. The frond can be undulate.

The sori are arranged in linear rows at the distal/apical 2/3rd to ¾ of the frond along the abaxial surface. There is no indusium.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Bulbostylis floccosa grows as a clumping perennial herb to 40 cm in height when in flower, with a roundish stem. Leaves small and plants essentially bladeless with photosynthetic stems.

The incomplete, perfect flowers are arranged in a terminal cluster of 2-5 flattened spikelets. The spikelets are at the end of a triangular shaped peduncle and are subtended by a bract which is an extension of the stem. The flowers are subtended by ovate, ciliate/pubescent, brown bracts with a yellow to green midvein. There is no calyx or corolla. There are 3 stamens. The ovary is superior with a single locule with a 3-parted style. The fruit is an obovate achene at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Carissa carandas grows as thin shrub up to 5 m in height. The stems have simple or forked spines to 3 cm in length. The coriaceous, glabrous leaves are arranged oppositely, to 6 cm long, 3 cm wide, ovate to oblong with and entire margin and an apiculate/emarginate leaf apex.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are solitary or in cymes in leaf axils. The calyx has 5 unfused, greenish sepals. The corolla has 5 white to light rose/pink petals that are fused forming a tube with the elongate lobes overlapping to one side forming a pinwheel shape and slightly pubescent to ciliate along the margins. There are 5 stamens fused to the corolla tube. The ovary is superior and has two locules and many ovules. The fruit is an oval dark red to black berry with a milky sap at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Ceiba pentandra grows as a deciduous tree to 4o m in height and 4 m in diameter producing buttress roots. Young branches and the trunk may be spiny/thorny. The palmately compound leaves are arranged alternately, with 5-15 leaflets. Each leaflet lanceolate to oblanceolate, to 20 cm long, entire to serrate.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are in axillary clusters that emerge while the tree is leafless. Flowers subtended by 7 - 9 green bracts. The calyx has 5 green, fused at base sepals that are interiorly pubescent. The corolla has 5, white to pink, fused at the base, pubescent petals. There are 5 stamens that are fused to the corolla. The ovary is superior with 5 locules and numerous ovules. The fruit is a pendulous woody capsule that is brown at maturity breaking apart rather than splitting along suture lines. The seeds are covered with long pubescence.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Combretum indicum grows as a climbing vine to 8 m in length. The leaves are arranged oppositely, oval/ovate and up to 15 cm in length, with an entire margin and an acuminate apex. The leaves are abaxially pubescent.

The complete, perfect, flowers occur in heads that are arranged in a a terminal or axillary spike. The calyx has 5 fused sepals. The corolla has 5 fused petals that start white and age to red. There are 10 stamens that are fused to the corolla. The inferior ovary has 1 locule and 3-4 ovules. At maturity the fruit is a dark red to brown winged/ridged drupe.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Chionanthus bumelioides grows as a tree up to 10 m in height (usually smaller). Young stems grey. The leaves are arranged oppositely, to 10 cm in length and 4 cm wide, elliptic to oblong, with an entire margin and an obtuse leaf apex.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in axillary and terminal panicles. The calyx has 4, green, unfused sepals. The corolla has 4 white unfused, petals. There are 2 stamens. The ovary is superior with 2 locules. The fruit is a dark blue drupe at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Chioccoca stricta grows as an erect shrub to 2 meters in height. The leaves are arranged oppositely, ovate to elliptic, to 4 cm in length, with an obtuse leaf apex and an entire margin. The stipules are connate with bristle teeth.

C. stricta differs from C. alba by having branches ascending rather than at 90-degree angles to the stem (C. alba).

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in few flowered racemes. The calyx has 5 unfused sepals. The corolla has 5 fused, white petals. There are 5 stamens. The ovary is inferior with 2 locules. The fruit is a compressed, few seeded, berry that is white at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description: Encyclia androsiana grow as an epiphyte. It produces a very short rhizomatous stem that is covered with secondary stems that are expanded to form ovate pseudobulbs up to 3 cm in length and 2.5 cm in width. From the top of the pseudobulb 1 flattened linear lanceolate leaf emerges that is up to 20 cm in length and 1.5 cm wide. The zygomorphic flowers are arranged in terminal panicles up to 25 cm in height and contains up to 15 flowers (usually much fewer). The flowers have triangular bracts and the calyx has 3 greenish yellow sepals that turn brownish with age. The corolla has 3 green to yellow petals with one forming the labellum. The sepals and petals develop spots with age. The labellum is white and 3 lobed. The central lobe is to 1.5 cm long, developing 2 major reddish-purple spots with red/purple lines at its base. The 2 lateral lobes of the labellum are white with radiating purple red lines at their base, erect to either side of the column, not clasping and open with the top of the column exposed. The column is formed from a fusion of the stamens and ovary into a single elongate structure. Along the bottom of the column between the lateral labellum lobes is an elongate callus plate with 2 lobes at the front edge with the yellow anthers. The top of the column develops purple lines and spots. The ovary is inferior. The fruit is a capsule at maturity up to 3 cm in length that opens along six suture lines and hangs pendulant, allowing wind to assist in seed dispersal.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Sideroxylon horridum grows as a large shrub to small tree up to 9 m in height. Young stems are brown pubescent. Branching pattern with stems at right angles. The leaves are arranged alternately (often clustered), to 4 cm in length (usually smaller), variable in shape from obovate with a flat or rounded leaf apex to elliptical with an acute leaf apex. The leaf margin is entire. Short branches occur as spines.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic, and subsessile flowers are arranged in groups of 1-4 arising in the axils of leaves. The calyx has 5 unfused brown pubescent sepals. The corolla has 5 white fused petals. There are 5 stamens fused to the corolla and numerous staminodes. The ovary is superior with 1 locule and seed. The fruit is a drupe at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Spermacoce brittonii Spermacoce brittonii grows as a glabrous perennial woody sub-shrub up to 40 cm in height. Branches quadrangular with the internodes longer than the leaf length. The leaves are arranged oppositely with short acute, slightly pubescent, stipules between the petioles. The sessile leaves are narrow elliptic to linear oblong up to 2 cm long (typically shorter) and 4 mm wide, with an acute leaf apex and an entire margin. Leaves shorter toward the branch apex.

The actinomorphic, perfect, complete, flowers occur in terminal heads at the ends of branches and are subtended by shorter leaves. The calyx has 4 fused at the base, glabrous ovate – lanceolate, lobed sepals. The corolla has 4 fused, glabrous, white, petals that form a short tube and each slightly recurved lobe with an ovate apex. There are 4 stamens that are fused to the perianth forming a hypanthium. The ovary is inferior with 1 locule and many ovules. The fruit is a capsule at maturity.
creator: Ethan Freid

description:
Adenium obesum grows as succulent shrub up to 3 m in height. The leaves are arranged alternately, obovate to oblinear, to 12 cm long, 4 cm wide, and clustered at branch tips. The leaves have an obtuse to acuminate leaf apex and an entire margin. The leaf surfaces pubescent or glabrous. Vegetation produces a milky sap.

The complete, perfect, actinomorphic flowers are arranged in corymbose panicles arising in leaf axils. The calyx has 5 unfused, greenish sepals. The corolla has 5 red, pink or white petals that are fused forming a tube with the lobes overlapping to one side forming a pinwheel shape. There are 5 stamens fused to the corolla tube. The ovary is superior and has two locules and many ovules. The fruit is a follicle (in pairs) that turns brown at maturity. The seeds have tufts of hairs at one end to assist in dispersal.
creator: Ethan Freid
